$comment: Reviewed evidence for the version 1 Handoff HTTP framing. Authored by hand from packages/adapters/http/protocol.ts and remote.ts, which every TypeScript mount already shares. This promotes an existing convention to a specified transport so a non-TypeScript host can serve it and a non-TypeScript client can reach it. A gate may verify these vectors but must never rewrite them.
$scope: Framing only: routes, methods, status mapping, cache validation, and the rejection envelope. Envelope identity is program.json and handoff-response.json; this vector never restates them.

routes.$comment: Exactly two routes under a host-chosen absolute base path. The base must not be the application root and carries no trailing slash. Anything else is 404.

manifest.$comment: The ETag is the binding digest in quotes, so a client revalidates against exact Binding identity rather than a timestamp. A replaced Installation produces a different digest and therefore a different ETag.

invoke.$comment: The request body is the bare HandoffInvocation envelope and the response body is the bare HandoffOutcome envelope. There is no wrapper object. A fault is still an outcome envelope; it is carried on a non-2xx status, and a client must read the envelope rather than infer meaning from the status alone.

statusForOutcome.name: declared-error
statusForOutcome.$note: 422, not 400: a declared error is a domain outcome the contract predicted, not a malformed request.

statusForOutcome.name: fault-revoked
statusForOutcome.$note: 409, so a client can distinguish a stale pin from a malformed request and re-handshake.

rejections.$comment: A rejection happens before an outcome exists, so it carries a diagnostic envelope instead. `kind` is `protocol` when the receiver recognized the failure and `internal` otherwise; an internal rejection never carries a path, because a path would leak host structure.

error.path: string, present only when kind is protocol

conflictStatusRule.$comment: A recognized rejection is 409 when the pin is stale rather than the request malformed, and 400 otherwise.
